rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-checked chunk 3's newly added clause (line 20, 'You can watch the smaller version of this already: as a shared rules file grows, agents start treating its sections as optional.'). 'This' resolves to the tax scenario named in the immediately preceding clause of the same bullet ('A company layer done wrong is a tax: memory loaded everywhere, owned by no one...'); 'its' resolves within-sentence to 'a shared rules file'. Both are same-bullet, same-sentence-flow antecedents — resolve cleanly, no forward pointer, no cross-file lean.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 header 'The hard part is the shape' still holds after the addition: the new clause supplies observable evidence for the shape-is-hard thesis (a smaller-scale instance of the same failure mode), and the bullet still lands on 'the smallest shared layer that survives contact with a real org' — the header's own claim, not contradicted or diluted by the insert.

New clause checked against all six sub-items: (a) 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction - absent, the clause is a single declarative plus a colon-led illustration. (b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples - not a triple structure. (c) Self-grading superlative - none ('the smaller version of this' is not a value-prop claim). (d) Number + own retraction - no numerals. (e) Abstraction-noun stack - 'the smaller version of this' leans abstract but is cashed out concretely in the same sentence ('as a shared rules file grows, agents start treating its sections as optional'), which is exactly the rule's own remedy, so it does not land as an uncashed stack. (f) Verb triplet with an empty leg - none. Pre-existing triad in the same bullet ('memory loaded everywhere, owned by no one, the CLAUDE.md equivalent of the staff handbook nobody reads') re-checked too: each leg adds distinct concrete content, not repetitive anaphora — holds.
